left_definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments rely on abstract normative principles (e.g. rights, fairness, morality, what ought to be) rather than specific institutional precedents?
left_spec: Parse OC_comments. For each comment decide if its main support is an abstract normative principle or value argument (e.g. fairness, liberty, justice, moral duty, 'people should') without citing a specific, functioning institutional precedent as its support. A comment that cites a specific functioning institutional precedent as its main support does not count; comments with neither (e.g. purely factual/personal/logical) do not count. Commenter's own assertions only; quotations count only if adopted. Use title/argument only to interpret the target. Ignore any OP view-change/delta announcements or outcome reports. Output = qualifying comments / total comments, in [0,1]. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null.
right_definition: What share of the counter-argument comments rely on abstract principles or general reasoning without any concrete, locally verifiable example?
right_spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Use title/argument only to interpret the comment's target. For each comment decide whether the commenter's own argument rests on abstract principles, general claims or hypothetical reasoning AND contains no concrete, specific, checkable example (specific case, event, figure or described particular situation). Quoted OP text or unadopted quoted background does not count as the commenter's own. Ignore view-change/delta announcements and post-outcome updates. Output = (comments meeting criterion)/(total comments), range 0-1. Empty list -> null; malformed/missing -> null. Comments that are neither (e.g. questions, off-topic) count in the denominator but not the numerator.

left_definition: Does the original poster's argument text contain at least one explicit admission of the OP's own uncertainty about their view or claims?
left_spec: Read only `argument` (OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP's own assertions include at least one explicit admission of uncertainty about their own position or claims (e.g., 'I'm not sure', 'I could be wrong', 'I'm unsure whether', 'I might be mistaken'). Return 0 if none. Generic hedging words without an admission of the OP's uncertainty do not count. Do not count uncertainty in quoted text attributed to others unless the OP adopts it as their own. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting that the view changed, post-outcome updates, or reports of the outcome; these are not evidence. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; empty text gives 0.
